C07 · 10 NOVEMBER 2026

Review register

Electronic comparison is complete for the existing 277 passages. It does not establish a definitive text. The complete books are not yet translated. Corrections follow identified evidence; conjectures and damaged readings remain visible.

Existing passages compared electronically277 / 277
Qurʾānic chapter blocks checked19 / 19
Complete Arabic passage transcriptions276 / 277
Fresh page-image collation0 / 277
Final scholarly approval0 / 277

Recovered C07 evidence: T108.04’s exact missing Arabic is retained in brackets from the earlier saved correction record, citing Dubai XVI:603. This resolves that transcription gap without claiming a fresh scan check. T113.06 remains incomplete in Arabic.

Remaining work

  • Obtain and collate complete printed-page images for every translated passage.

  • Resolve all flagged variants and verify the Arabic lacuna in T113.06.

  • Translate and review the remainder of Tibi on Fatiha I:687–770.

  • Collate additional witnesses before claiming a definitive critical text.

  • Complete independent scholarly review, citations, report/poem attribution and remaining lexical checks.

  • The Kashshaf closing prayer/colophon and Tibi epilogue remain outside the current reader.

  • segment id

    T099.01

    kind

    open_textual_crux

    detail

    The electronic Tibi witness reads جزعال التي تطلع (and قصطال). Classical primary lexica give خَزْعال, lameness, in ناقة بها خزعال أي ظلع, followed by the same discussion of qahqar and qastal. This is strong lexical evidence for corruption, but it does not establish what Tibi or this print actually reads. Do not silently emend to خزعال التي تظلع or label the issue resolved. Current jizʿāl adds an unsupported kasra contrary to the faʿlāl discussion; current “printed text” claim exceeds this audit.

    evidence
    • url
      https://quranpedia.app/books/futuh-ghayb/s511.html
      page

      XVI:536

      line
      22
    • url
      https://www.islamweb.net/ar/library/content/122/2170/خزعل
      work

      Lisan al-Arab, خزعل

      text

      وناقة بها خزعال أي ظلع ... قال الفراء: وليس في الكلام فعلال مفتوح الفاء من غير ذوات التضعيف إلا حرف واحد

    • url
      https://arabiclexicon.hawramani.com/خَزْعَلَ/?book=21
      work

      al-Sihah, خزعل

      text

      وناقة بها خزعال، أي ظلع

    recommended note

    The electronic text reads جزعال التي تطلع. Compare the lexicographical خَزْعال, “lameness”; “limps” is a conjectural recovery of the intended sense, pending direct collation of Tibi and al-Kawashi.

normalization policy
structural

Remove retrieval line markers, navigation, page numbers from running Arabic, OpenITI markers, detached footnote callouts. Join only the selected authorial layer. Whitespace normalized; the Arabic raw field retains substantive electronic readings.

typography

Every editorial typo/glyph repair is listed separately. Some electronic punctuation/bracket artifacts remain. The malformed T094.09 clause and T099.01 crux remain uncorrected. These transcriptions are not scan-perfect Arabic.

display recommendation

Show electronic-text status and unresolved reading notes; use arabic_raw for checking the source and arabic only as a documented edited transcription. A separate Quran header may be supplied by the parent without treating it as an authorial Arabic witness.

    واستحقاق المدح إنما يحصل برؤية الكيفيات لا برؤية الذوات

    reason

    يحصل describes the arising of entitlement to praise; the current discerned supplies an epistemic verb absent from the Arabic. The abstract phrasing avoids supplying an unstated subject of entitlement, and the contrast between كيفيات and ذوات is preserved.

  • Hadith reports are translated as the authors give them; this audit does not authenticate every transmission.

                                    • old

                                      ownership (milk, مِلْك) is general, whereas kingship (mulk, مُلْك) is particular

                                      new

                                      kingship (mulk, مُلْك) is general, whereas ownership (milk, مِلْك) is particular

                                      reason

                                      Existing rendering reverses the two nouns. Al-Jurjānī’s primary ḥāshiya explicitly reads الملك بالضم يعم والملك بالكسر يخص; Ṭībī’s corresponding lemma is also vocalized المُلك يعم، والمِلك يخص.

                                      category

                                      material_translation_error

                                      evidence source ids

                                      • Jurjani-Hasiya-I57

                                    notes

                                    • The electronic Kashshāf text here leaves the two الملك nouns unvocalized. The English correction is grounded in the explicitly vocalized/commented primary gloss, rather than guessed from the consonants.

                                    • K001.12–13 are supplied entirely from the separate K-QuranTafsir-1-4 witness because the local OpenITI text jumps from أبو حنيفة to على اختصاص الحمد. These additions are not falsely attributed to the defective local passage.

                                    • The supplemental witness displays مَلَك after وقرأ غيره, whereas the English interprets malika, the accusative form of malik. Preserve the electronic form and flag its vocalization for scan comparison; this audit does not certify all short vowels.

                                                                                            T094.01

                                                                                            kind

                                                                                            revised_translation

                                                                                            before

                                                                                            On “it affirms and establishes the expansion”: He repudiates the absence of expansion. Once that absence is repudiated, expansion is established, because the interrogative hamza expresses repudiation; repudiation is negation, and negation applied to negation becomes affirmation. The hamza may not be treated here as a question seeking acknowledgment (taqrīr).

                                                                                            after

                                                                                            Meccan; eight verses. In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Merciful.

                                                                                            On “it affirms and establishes the expansion”: He repudiates the absence of expansion. Once that absence is repudiated, expansion is established, because the interrogative hamza expresses repudiation; repudiation is negation, and negation applied to negation becomes affirmation. The hamza may not be treated here as a question seeking acknowledgment (taqrīr).

                                                                                          • id

                                                                                            T094.04

                                                                                            kind

                                                                                            revised_translation

                                                                                            before

                                                                                            On “he read a-lam nashraḥa, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ”: its original form is nashraḥan. The nūn was omitted and the fatḥa on the ḥāʾ retained as an indication of it. This is in al-Muntaqā. Ibn Jinnī said: “A-lam nashraḥa, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, is transmitted from Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr. Ibn Mujāhid said: ‘This is wholly impermissible.’” Ibn Jinnī said: “The obvious position, and what accords with customary usage, is as Ibn Mujāhid states. Something like it nevertheless occurs in what I read to Abū ʿAlī in Abū Zayd's Nawādir: ‘From which of death's two days shall I flee— a day not decreed, or a day decreed?’ It is said that he intended lam yuqdar-an, with the light emphatic nūn. In our view omitting it is impermissible, because the emphatic nūn is most closely allied to expansion and elaboration, not concision and abbreviation. In Abū Zayd's Nawādir there is another verse, said to be fabricated: ‘Strike away the anxieties that visit you by night, as with a sword you strike a horse's forelock.’ He intended iḍrib-an, with the light nūn, and omitted it.”

                                                                                            after

                                                                                            On “he read a-lam nashraḥa, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ”: its original form is nashraḥan. The nūn was omitted and the fatḥa on the ḥāʾ retained as an indication of it. This is in al-Muntaqā. Ibn Jinnī said: “A-lam nashraḥa, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, is transmitted from Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr. Ibn Mujāhid said: ‘This is wholly impermissible.’” Ibn Jinnī said: “The obvious position, and what accords with customary usage, is as Ibn Mujāhid states. Something like it nevertheless occurs in what I read to Abū ʿAlī in Abū Zayd's Nawādir: ‘From which of death's two days shall I flee— a day not decreed, or a day decreed?’ It is said that he intended lam yuqdar-an, with the light emphatic nūn. In our view omitting it is impermissible, because the emphatic nūn is most closely allied to expansion and elaboration, not concision and abbreviation. In Abū Zayd's Nawādir there is another verse, said to be fabricated: ‘Strike away the anxieties that visit you by night, as with a sword you strike the crown of a horse's head.’ He intended iḍrib-an, with the light nūn, and omitted it.”

                                                                                            T095.02

                                                                                            kind

                                                                                            revised_translation

                                                                                            before

                                                                                            On “removes decay”: one says ḥafirat asnānuhu ḥafaran when the sockets of his teeth—that is, their roots—have deteriorated. One also says ḥafarat ḥafran; ḥafra denotes a single occurrence.

                                                                                            after

                                                                                            On “removes decay”: one says ḥafirat asnānuhu ḥafaran when the sockets of his teeth—that is, their roots—have deteriorated. One also says ḥafarat ḥafran; ḥafra denotes a single occurrence.

                                                                                            On “and so is amīn; ammān is also said”: that is, they use ammān (أمان) in place of amīn (أمين).

                                                                                          Adopted correction record

                                                                                          • id

                                                                                            T097.05

                                                                                            kind

                                                                                            revised_translation

                                                                                            before

                                                                                            On “it is nothing but safety”: he means that hiya, “it,” is the subject and salām, “peace,” the predicate. The predicate is placed first, and the night is made peace itself, to convey exclusivity.

                                                                                            The author of al-Kashf says: “Hiya is a subject and salām a preceding predicate. Salām has the sense of an active participle: it brings peace. This interpretation is necessary if ḥattā, ‘until,’ is to depend on it. If salām were taken as a verbal noun, ḥattā could not depend on it, because one may not separate a governing expression from its complement. It may instead depend on ‘the angels descend.’ Hiya cannot be the subject with the phrase beginning ḥattā as its predicate, for that would convey no useful information: every night has this characteristic [of lasting until dawn].”

                                                                                            after

                                                                                            On “it is nothing but safety”: he means that hiya, “it,” is the subject and salām, “peace,” the predicate. The predicate is placed first, and the night is made peace itself, to convey exclusivity.

                                                                                            The author of al-Kashf says: “Hiya is a subject and salām a preceding predicate. Salām has the sense of an active participle: it brings peace. This interpretation is necessary if ḥattā, ‘until,’ is to depend on it. If salām were taken as a verbal noun, ḥattā could not depend on it, because the verbal noun may not be separated from its dependent complement [here by hiya]. It may instead depend on ‘the angels descend.’ Hiya cannot be the subject with the phrase beginning ḥattā as its predicate, for that would convey no useful information: every night has this characteristic [of lasting until dawn].”

                                                                                            K099.02

                                                                                            kind

                                                                                            revised_translation

                                                                                            before

                                                                                            Zilzālahā is read with kasra or fatḥa on the zāy. With kasra it is a verbal noun; with fatḥa, a noun. Among word-patterns, faʿlāl with fatḥa occurs only in a reduplicated form.

                                                                                            If you ask what “its shaking” means in the possessive construction, I answer: the shaking that befits it in accordance with wisdom and God’s will—the violent shaking beyond which there is none. Compare: “Honour the pious man with his honour, and abase the impious man with his abasement,” meaning the honour and abasement they respectively deserve. Or it means its entire shaking, every degree of shaking possible for it.

                                                                                            Athqāl is the plural of thiql, household goods, as in “They carry your burdens” [16:7]. He makes the things buried within the earth its burdens.

                                                                                            after

                                                                                            Zilzālahā is read with kasra or fatḥa on the zāy. With kasra it is a verbal noun; with fatḥa, a noun. Among word-patterns, faʿlāl with fatḥa occurs only in a reduplicated form.

                                                                                            If you ask what “its shaking” means in the possessive construction, I answer: the shaking that befits it in accordance with wisdom and God’s will—the violent shaking beyond which there is none. Compare: “Honour the pious man with his honour, and abase the impious man with his abasement,” meaning the honour and abasement they respectively deserve. Or it means its entire shaking, every degree of shaking possible for it.

                                                                                            Athqāl is the plural of thaqal (ثَقَل), household goods, as in “They carry your burdens” [16:7]. He makes the things buried within the earth its burdens.

                                                                                            T099.01

                                                                                            kind

                                                                                            revised_translation

                                                                                            before

                                                                                            Medinan; nine verses. In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Merciful. [The embedded Kashshāf heading instead records disagreement about the place of revelation; both headings here give nine verses.]

                                                                                            On “among word-patterns, faʿlāl with fatḥa occurs only in a reduplicated form,” al-Kawāshī has: “Nāqa jizʿāl occurs, meaning a she-camel which [limps; the printed text here reads ‘looks out/climbs’], as does qasṭāl, a word for dust; neither is reduplicated. It is said that Bahrām and Shahrām are foreign.” As for qahqār, it is a weak linguistic form. Al-Ṣiḥāḥ has: “Qahqarr, with doubled rāʾ, is hard stone. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā alone used to say qahqār.”

                                                                                            after

                                                                                            Medinan; nine verses. In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Merciful. [The embedded Kashshāf heading instead records disagreement about the place of revelation; both headings here give nine verses.]

                                                                                            On “among word-patterns, faʿlāl with fatḥa occurs only in a reduplicated form,” al-Kawāshī has: “The expression nāqa جزعال occurs, meaning a she-camel which [probably ‘limps’; the electronic text reads تطلع, ‘looks out/climbs’], as does qasṭāl, a word for dust; neither is reduplicated. It is said that Bahrām and Shahrām are foreign.” As for qahqār, it is a weak linguistic form. Al-Ṣiḥāḥ has: “Qahqarr, with doubled rāʾ, is hard stone. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā alone used to say qahqār.”

                                                                                                                                                                      T105.05

                                                                                                                                                                      status

                                                                                                                                                                      recommended_precision_correction

                                                                                                                                                                      old

                                                                                                                                                                      Desert of praise is discerned by seeing modes, not merely entities.

                                                                                                                                                                      arabic evidence

                                                                                                                                                                      واستحقاق المدح إنما يحصل برؤية الكيفيات لا برؤية الذوات

                                                                                                                                                                      reason

                                                                                                                                                                      يحصل describes the arising of entitlement to praise; the current discerned supplies an epistemic verb absent from the Arabic. The abstract phrasing avoids supplying an unstated subject of entitlement, and the contrast between كيفيات and ذوات is preserved.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • old

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              tabban lahu and tabba lahu

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              new

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              tabban lahu (تَبًّا له) and tabbun lahu (تَبٌّ له)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              evidence

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              s519 line25 explicitly contrasts accusative and nominative nouns: تبًّا له وتبٌّ له. tabba falsely represents the second as a finite verb.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • old

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              ʿajizat and ʿajjazat

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              ʿajazat (عَجَزَتْ) and ʿajjazat (عَجَّزَتْ)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              evidence

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              s519 line27 vocalizes عَجَزَت with fatḥa on jīm, whereas existing transliteration has kasra. This aligns this witness, not a claim that no alternate lexical form exists.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              arabic

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              يقول: عزمت على الإقامة إلى وقت الصباح لأني قد وجدت الرأي والحزم قد أوجبا ذلك

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              [SOURCE CHECK T112-U3: Al-Baghdādī, Khizānat al-adab III:86–88, records the full line and explains إقامة ذي صباح as remaining until morning.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               reason

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        while remaining sound in his prophetic capacity. It would impair prophethood only [if]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        after

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        [and recovered, inasmuch as he was human, not inasmuch as he was a prophet]. It would impair prophethood only [if]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        reason

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Al-Raghib's quoted source has ويمرض ويصح من حيث هو بشر لا من حيث هو نبي and لو وجد للسحر تأثير. The existing provisional reading gives صح a different syntactic role. Brackets show restoration from the quotation source.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        arabic

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        ويمرض ويصح من حيث هو بشر لا من حيث هو نبي، وإنما كان ذلك قادحا في النبوة لو وجد للسحر تأثير في أمر يرجع إلى النبوة

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        status

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        recommended

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      • before

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        [REVIEW T113-U2: The scan p.648 reads فيصح من حيث نبي and then أو وجد للسحر تأثير. The first is provisionally read as preservation of prophetic soundness; “[if]” expresses the apparently intended conditional of the second, whose printed أو is problematic. Check al-Rāghib's source before removing the flag. At p.649 the scan has بما يقع, correcting OpenITI's بما لا يقع, which reverses the argument.]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        after

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        [SOURCE CHECK T113-U2: The earlier scan report gives فيصح من حيث نبي and أو وجد للسحر تأثير. Al-Rāghib's own tafsīr of 2:102 reads ويمرض ويصح من حيث هو بشر لا من حيث هو نبي and لو وجد للسحر تأثير. The bracketed restoration follows the quoted source and explains the human capacity in which illness and recovery occur. The same source confirms the positive بما يقع, already reported from Dubai XVI:649. Ṭībī's exact damaged wording still requires another witness; no new scan collation is claimed.]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        reason

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The quoted source resolves the intended contrast and conditional without erasing the Tibi witness problem.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          recommended

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        • before

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          [REVIEW T114-U3: The final sentence is problematic in the print itself: وهذا القول المتعسف لا يريد أنه ضعيف. Its wording is retained, even though its denial of weakness conflicts with the following criticism. The phrase لا يريد may be displaced from the next gloss; that is a hypothesis, not an adopted correction. Check the Imam's source before repairing it. Mā in وما أحقه is negative, not an exclamation; the scan, Ṭībī's gloss and Turkish p.1480 agree.]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          after

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          [SOURCE CHECK T114-U3: The earlier scan report gives وهذا القول المتعسف لا يريد أنه ضعيف. Al-Rāzī's tafsīr of 114:6 instead reads وهذا القول ضعيف, followed by the same linguistic objection. This confirms that the source criticizes the interpretation, but does not establish how the corruption arose in Ṭībī. The printed wording is retained with this warning; displacement from the next gloss remains a hypothesis. Mā in وما أحقه is negative, not exclamatory.]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          reason

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Primary quoted source establishes intended criticism but not exact Tibi emendation.
